marta: Heads-up — canary for customer-facing endpoint (gptx-3.1-b2) shows a clear perf regression after the model onboard/config bump earlier today. 95p latency up ~40% on short-seq workloads (<=64).

aj: ugh, live? numbers from CI or staging traces?

marta: staging traces + our perf CI both show it. CI summary: tests/perf/latency: baseline 14ms p95 -> now 20ms p95 (short seq). embedding throughput OK.

aj: can you paste profiling? kernel selection, batching logs, KV cache stats?

devon: pasting profiler excerpt — looks like kernel fallback to matmul_v2 (slower for short seqs) and KV cache miss spikes. not a pure model weight perf issue, seems runtime path change.

```
# PERF SNAPSHOT (staging-canary)
request_type: text_generation
seq_len_hist: {mean: 18, p95: 62}
kernel_chosen: matmul_v2 (hotpath), previous: matmul_v1
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78 -> 0.52
batching_policy: adaptive(default) -> grouped_by_len
cpu: negligible, gpu_util: normal
```

marta: interesting — the model onboarding JSON included a tokenizer config tweak: "add_bos": true and "preserve_spaces": false. That increases token counts for short prompts (extra prefix), so runtime path picked a different kernel and grouping heuristic changed.

ryan: iirc the kernel selector branches based on estimated active_k (tokens*batch_size) and uses matmul_v2 for >2048 flops to better saturate big kernels. small-seq regime used v1 which is faster for short sequences. If token counts shift up a bit we can cross the threshold.

aj: that aligns with batching logs: batching heuristic switched from continuous-batching to grouped_by_len for this model. grouped_by_len causes less cross-request KV reuse, so KV cache misses go up.

marta: we ran a quick bisect across recent commits — culprit is PR #3421 (tokenizer: normalize_unicode + add_bos) landed in model-onboard branch. Repro steps attached in the onboarding PR.

devon: reproduced locally: revert of the tokenizer lines restores p95 to baseline. kernel selection returns to matmul_v1, KV hit rate back to 0.82.

ci-bot: perf/regression check failed on 1765432087 (gptx-3.1-b2) — delta +38% p95. See https://ci.internal/perf/1765432087

aj: since this is a canary-blocker and rollout is blocked, we have two options: 1) revert PR 3421 (fast) or 2) adjust runtime heuristics to be robust to small tokenizer drift (longer-term). I vote revert + test.

ryan: Agreed. Also we should add a small integration test that simulates the tokenizer producing an extra BOS token and asserts kernel selection + KV hit rate don't degrade more than 5%.

marta: I'll open the revert PR now and add a follow-up issue for heuristic hardening + onboarding checklist item.

devon: note for postmortem: model config drift (tokenizer) changed tokenization distribution enough to flip kernel selection thresholds and batching mode -> KV cache durability dropped. Root cause is onboarding config not covered by our perf-unit tests.

aj: action items: 
- marta: revert PR3421 and block rollout (if not already).
- ryan/devon: add regression test + a perf-canary job exercising short-seq workload for every model-onboard change.
- infra: consider making kernel-selection thresholds a tunable we can override per-model until tokenizer is stable.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: revert PR 3421 queued, estimated cool-down 2m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

marta: thanks — will follow up with issue + assign owners. tagging @product to keep them aware (will impact onboarding timeline). :thumbsup:

aj: postmortem template: brief timeline, root cause (tokenizer config drift -> kernel/batching heuristic flip -> KV cache miss), mitigation (revert, tests, heuristic tunable), owner list, and steps to prevent recurrence.

devon: i'll attach profiler traces and a minimal repro script to the issue.

marta: closing the thread once revert finishes and perf CI is green.
